 
Medical  Spelling  Event  Category:  Health  Science
…………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………
 
Eligible  Divisions:  Secondary  &  Postsecondary/  Collegiate  
Round  One:  50  Q  test  (60  minutes)  Digital  Upload:  NO  
Solo  Event:  1  competitor  Round  Two:  Spelldown  
New  for  2026-2027
 Editorial  changes  have  been  made.    
Event  Summary
 Medical  Spelling  allows  HOSA  members  to  gain  knowledge  and  skills  regarding  the  deﬁnitions  and  spelling  of  medical  terms.  
This
 
competitive
 
event
 
consists
 
of
 
two
 
rounds:
 
Round
 
One
 
is
 
a
 
written,
 
multiple-choice
 
test,
 
and
 
Round
 
Two
 
is
 
a
 
“spelldown”
 
in
 
which
 
competitors
 
spell
 
terms
 
in
 
front
 
of
 
judges.
 
This
 
event
 
aims
 
to
 
inspire
 
members
 
to
 
become
 
skilled
 
in
 
medical
 
spelling.
 
 
General  Event  Information
 
General  Rules   Competitors  must  be  familiar  with  and  adhere  to  the  General  Rules  and  Regulations.  
Dress  Code  Proper  business  attire  or  ofﬁcial  HOSA  uniform.  Bonus  points  will  be  awarded  for  proper  dress.   Competitors  not  dressed  appropriately  for  Round  Two  will  not  be  allowed  to  compete.  
Competitors  Must  Provide  ●  A  photo  ID for  both  rounds   ●  Two  #2  lead  pencils  (not  mechanical)  with  eraser  for  the  test.  ●  Neon  colored  foam  earplugs,  NOT  earbuds,  for  noise  control  (Rd1-optional)  HOSA  Conference  Staff  will  provide  equipment  and  supplies  listed  in  Appendix  I.  
Ofﬁcial  References   The  references  below  are  used  in  the  development  of  the  test  questions and  spelling  lists:  ●  Taber's  Cyclopedic  Medical  Dictionary .  Edited  by  Donald  Venes  and   Clayton  L.  Thomas,  M.D   F.A.  Davis  Company,   Latest  edition. ●  Taber’s  Audio  Glossary,  F.A.  Davis  Company,  Latest  edition. ●  Purchasing  the  dictionary  will  also  give  HOSA  members  access  to  the  audio  online  glossary,  which  can  be  used  by  Chartered  Associations/ILC  for  competition  and  by  competitors  to  practice.   
ROUND  ONE-  Test
 
Test  Instructions  All  competitors  will  be  given  a  test  and  test  answer  sheet.  The  written  test  will  consist  of  50  multiple-choice  items  in  a  maximum  of  60  minutes.  See  test  instructions  here. 
Time  Remaining  Announcements  
There  will  be  NO  verbal  announcements  for  time  remaining  during  ILC  testing.   All  ILC  testing  will  be  completed  in  the  Testing  Center,  and  competitors  are  responsible  for  monitoring  their  own  time.  
  
 Medical  Spelling  ILC  Guidelines  (September  2026)         Page  1  of  5  The  expectation  is  that  competitors  read  and  are  aware  of  all  the  content  within  these  guidelines  and  associated  links.  Successful  competitors  will  study  all  links  for  the  detailed  information.   

 Sample  Test  Questions  1.  An  obstructing  infection  in  a  renal  pelvis  or  ureter  (Taber’s  pp  1973)  A.   Pilonefritis  B.   Pyonephrosis  C.   Pilonephritis  D.   Pyonefrosis  2.  A  specialist  in  diseases  of  the  nervous  system  (Taber’s  pp  1627)  A.   Neuralogist   B.   Neologist  C.   Neurologist  D.   Nurologist  3.  The  act  of  swallowing  (Taber’s  pp  631)   A.   Deglutition  B.   Digluation  C.   Deglutation  D.   Diglutition  
ROUND  TWO-  Spelldown
 
1.  The  top  competitors  from  Round  One  will  advance  to  Round  Two.  The  number  of  advancing  competitors  will  be  determined  by  the  scores  obtained  in  Round  One  and  the  space  and  time  available  for  Round  Two.  Round  Two  ﬁnalists  will  be  announced  on-site  at  ILC  per  the  conference  agenda.  
2.  If  the  competitor  is  more  than  ﬁve  (5)  minutes  late  to  Round  Two,  the  spelldown  will  begin  without  them,  and  they  may  not  be  allowed  to  compete  per  the  GRR.  
3.  Based  on  the  written  test  scores,  Round  Two  competitors  will  be  seated  in  ascending  order  (from  lowest  to  highest  test  scores)  for  the  spelldown.  The  spelldown  begins  with  the  competitor  with  the  lowest  test  score  seated  in  chair  #1.   
4.  The  “spelldown”  term  list  will  be  arranged  from  easy  to  complex.      Round  2,  numbered  1-50,  will  be  easy  terms.    Round  3,  numbered  1-50,  will  be  moderate  terms.   Round  4,  numbered  1-50,  will  be  complex  terms.   Round  5,  numbered  1-50,  will  be  complicated  terms.   
5.  Round  Two  competitors  shall  spell  terms  in  numerical  order  from  the  set  word  list  for  the  given  round.   
6.  AUDIO  PRONUNCIATION  OF  THE  WORD:  At  ILC,  Taber’s  Audio  Glossary  will  be  used  to  pronounce  each  term  for  the  competitor.  Competitors  can  use  the  audio  glossary  listed  in  the  Ofﬁcial  References  above to  practice.  Using  the  online  glossary  to  pronounce  each  term  will  ensure  everyone  hears  the  same  thing  across  all  sections.  Click  HERE for  a  sample  of  how  the  words  will  be  pronounced.  The  competitor  may  request  the  term  be  re-pronounced  by  the  Audio  Glossary  or  moderator  a  maximum  of  three  (3)  total  times.  
7.  COMPETITOR  PRONUNCIATION  OF  THE  WORD:  The  competitor  is  to  pronounce  the  term  given  to  him/her  and  pause  before  starting  to  spell  the  word .   This  will  allow  the  moderator  and  judge(s)  to  correct  the  competitor  IF  the  term  was  misunderstood.  If  the  competitor  mispronounces  the  term,  the  moderator  may  play  the  audio  term  again  and  also  pronounce  the  term  for  the  competitor.  The  competitor  is  NOT  ALLOWED  to  ask  the  judges  if  they  pronounced  the  word  correctly  -  the  judges  will  STOP  the  competitor  if  it  is  pronounced  incorrectly.  If  the  judges  do  not  stop  the  competitor,  the  competitor  can  assume  they  pronounced  the  word  correctly.     a.  The  best  time  for  the  judges  and  moderator  to  encourage  the  competitor  to  speak  louder  and  clearer  is  when  the  competitor  pronounces  the  word  before  they  begin  spelling.   For  example,  it  is  acceptable  for  the  judge  to  say,  “ STOP.   Please  repeat  your  pronunciation,  and  speak  loudly  and  clearly  as  you  spell  the  word.   We  want  to  
 Medical  Spelling  ILC  Guidelines  (September  2026)         Page  2  of  5  The  expectation  is  that  competitors  read  and  are  aware  of  all  the  content  within  these  guidelines  and  associated  links.  Successful  competitors  will  study  all  links  for  the  detailed  information.   
 be  sure  we  hear  exactly  what  you  are  spelling.”  The  competitor's  pronunciation  will  not  have  any  bearing  on  the  qualiﬁcation  or  elimination  of  any  competitor.  
8.  DEFINE  THE  WORD:  The  competitor  may  also  request  a  term  deﬁnition.  One  judge  or  moderator  should  be  designated  to  deﬁne  the  term  upon  request.  If  a  competitor  requests  a  deﬁnition,  the  designated  judge  or  moderator  should  read  the  dictionary  deﬁnition,  or  essential  part  of  the  deﬁnition,  aloud  to  the  competitor.  
9.  COMPETITOR  SPELLING  RESPONSIBILITIES:    a.  The  competitor  will  have  two  (2)  minutes  to  complete  spelling  the  term.   The  competitor  will  be  eliminated  if  the  spelling  has  not  been  completed  by  the  end  of  two  (2)  minutes.  The  time  will  begin  with  the  ﬁrst  pronunciation  by  the  audio  glossary.  b.  No  pen/pencil  or  paper  will  be  allowed  in  the  spelldown  for  the  competitor.  c.  During  the  two  (2)  minutes  and  before  starting  to  spell  the  word,  the  competitor  may  ask  for  as  many  as  three  (3)  additional  pronunciations  from  the  Audio  Glossary  OR  moderator  (3  total  pronunciations  between  audio  glossary/moderator,  NOT  3  pronunciations  by  EACH)   and  may  ask  for  another  deﬁnition,  but  the  clock  will  be  running.  d.  Once  spelling  has  begun,  there  will  be  no  other  opportunity  for  pronunciation  or  deﬁnition.    e.  After  starting  to  spell  the  term,  the  competitor  will  be  given  one  (1)  opportunity  to  change  letters.    f.  If  a  medical  term  provided  to  the  student  contains  a  hyphen,  the  competitor  will  state  “hyphen”  in  the  word's  appropriate  place.   If  the  medical  term  is  two  words,  the  competitor  must  state  “space”  in  the  appropriate  place  between  words.  If  the  term  provided  contains  an  apostrophe,  the  competitor  will  state  “apostrophe”  in  the  proper  place  in  the  word.   Competitors  will  not  be  penalized  if  capitalizations  are  not  included.    g.  A  warning  will  be  given  when 30  seconds  remain.   h.  The  competitor  must  pronounce  the  term again  to  declare  that  they  have  ﬁnished  spelling.   i.  If  the  competitor  fails  to  pronounce  the  term  before  spelling  or  after  spelling  the  term,   they  will  be  eliminated.  j.  The  moderator  will  NOT  give  the  correct  spelling  for  a  term  if  the  competitor  spells  the  term  incorrectly.  
10.  Judges  will  write  each  letter  as  the  competitor  spells  the  term.  If  there  are  doubts  about  the  spelling,  judges  will  wait  until  after  the  spelling  is  completed  and  confer.   If  there  is  still  confusion,  the  determination  may  be  made  to  have  the  competitor  respell  the  word  or give  the  competitor  a  new  word.   a.  JUDGE  TIP:  Be  aware  that  sometimes  there  are  two  correct  spellings  for  a  single  term.  Multiple  spellings  will  be  included  in  the  word  listing  the  judges  receive.  For  example:  ●  orthopedic    and    orthopaedic  ●  mammaplasty  and   mammoplasty  ●  malacoplakia  and   malakoplakia  ●  chakra   and    cakra  
11.  The  next  competitor  will  be  given  a  new  term  to  spell.   If  all  competitors  are  eliminated  in  a  single  round,  all  competitors  will  return  to  resume  the  spelldown.   If  only  one  competitor  spells  correctly  in  a  given  round  they  will  be  determined  the  winner.  Those  eliminated  will  return  to  a  spell  down  to  determine  the  remaining  top  ten.  
12.  The  elimination  procedure  changes  when  there  are  only  two  remaining  competitors:  a.  As  soon  as  one  competitor  misspells  a  term,  the  other  competitor  immediately  has  the  opportunity  to  spell  the  same  term.  b.  If  the  second  competitor  spells  the  term  correctly,  they  are  given  a  new  term.  c.  If  the  competitor  then  spells  the  new  term  correctly,  they  shall  be  declared  the  ﬁrst  place  Winner.  d.  However,  if  after  correctly  spelling  the  missed  term,  the  competitor  misspells  the  new  term,  a  new  round  with  new  terms  will  begin  with  both  competitors  spelling  in  the  original  order.  
13.  Any  question  relating  to  the  competition  must  be  referred  to  the  judges  immediately.  By  raising  their  hand,  the  competitor  will  be  recognized  by  the  event  personnel  or  judges.   The  decision  of  the  judges  is  ﬁnal.  
 Medical  Spelling  ILC  Guidelines  (September  2026)         Page  3  of  5  The  expectation  is  that  competitors  read  and  are  aware  of  all  the  content  within  these  guidelines  and  associated  links.  Successful  competitors  will  study  all  links  for  the  detailed  information.   
 14.  No  microphones  will  be  used  during  the  competition.  NO  OBSERVERS  will  be  allowed  during  the  event.  
15.  At  the  end  of  each  round,  eliminated  competitors  will  be  asked  to  leave  the  event  room.   a.  OPTIONAL  -  At  the  discretion  of  the  event  management,  a  restroom  break  may  be  given  at  the  end  of  speciﬁed  rounds.  At  the  end  of  each  round,  it  may  be  acceptable  to  clap  for  completed  competitors  and  then  escort  eliminated  competitors  from  the  room.   
Final  Scoring 
 
1.  If  the  ﬁnal  two  spellers  (or  any  number  deemed  appropriate  by  event  staff)  continue  to  go  back  and  forth  spelling  words  correctly  –  the  following  process  may  be  used:   a.  When  ﬁve  minutes  remain  in  the  event,  the  moderator  will  announce  the  remaining  time.  (Each  Chartered  Association  and  ILC  determines  the  time  dedicated  to  the  entire  Medical  Spelling  event  and  aligns  it  with  conference  planning  logistics.)   b.  If  the  ﬁnal  spellers  are  still  “standing”  at  the  end  of  the  given  time,  the  test  scores  will  be  used  as  the  tiebreaker.  The  competitor  with  the  highest  test  score  will  be  declared  the  winner.    ■  If  test  scores  are  the  same,  the  competitors  with  the  highest  test  scores  will  be  identiﬁed  as  co-winners.   ■  If  this  scenario  takes  place  at  a  Chartered  Association-level  competition,  the  Chartered  Association  will  most  likely  advance  the  co-winners  plus  the  3
 rd
 place  ﬁnisher  to  ILC;  however,  the  Chartered  Association  ultimately  makes  that  decision  on  a  case-by-case  basis.  
Spelldown  Results  Form  -  Instructions for  Event  Personnel  (form  is  on  page  5)  ●  Competitors  for  Round  Two  should  be  posted  in  the  order  they  will  spell,  beginning  with  the  competitor  qualiﬁed  for  Round  Two  with  the  lowest  test  score.  The  competitor  with  the  highest  test  score  from  Round  one  will  spell  last.   ●  Determine  how  many  spellers  are  in  Round  Two,  and  cross  out  the  places  not  needed  on  the  Spelldown  Results  page.  For  example  if  you  have  25  spellers,  cross  out  numbers  26-30.   ●  As  soon  as  the  ﬁrst  competitor  misspells  a  word,  their  competitor  number  should  be  written  in  the  last  row  of  the  Spelldown  Results  page.  (If  you  have  25  spellers,  write  the  number  of  the  ﬁrst  competitor  to  misspell  a  word  in  row  #25).   ●  Continue  to  ﬁll  in  the  results  each  time  a  competitor  misspells  a  word.   ●  The  last  remaining  competitor’s  ID  number  (winner)  will  be  written  in  row  #1  on  the  page.   ●  Complete  the  Spelldown  Results  page  information  (competitor  ID,  name,  school,  Charter  Association)  at  the  conclusion  of  the  event.   
Final  Opportunities  The  HOSA  Scholarship  program  has  funding  available  for  HOSA  members  who  have  an  interest  in  various  health  careers!   The  application  process  begins  January  1,  2027,  and  can  be  found  here: https://hosa.org/scholarships/.   Graduating  from  high  school  or  completing  your  postsecondary/collegiate  program  does  not  mean  your  HOSA  journey  has  to  
end.
